props.title: Stir of Echoes
props.initialSlug: Man's psychic awakening reveals a ghost's dark truth

sections.content: Released in the shadow of The Sixth Sense (1999), Stir of Echoes (1999) delivers a grittier, working-class take on supernatural horror. David Koepp's adaptation of Richard Matheson's novel centers on Tom Witzky (Kevin Bacon), a Chicago telephone lineman who becomes psychically awakened through hypnosis. Unlike the polished suburbs of The Sixth Sense (1999) or the gothic mansions of The Changeling (1980), this ghost story unfolds in blue-collar neighborhoods where financial struggles are as real as spectral visitors. The film's authentic Chicago setting and Bacon's raw performance ground the supernatural elements in a tangible reality. movies.title: The Sixth Sense
movies.slug: A child psychologist discovers his young patient can see dead people, leading to a shocking revelation

sections.content: Koepp's direction creates a suffocating atmosphere through creative visual techniques that mirror Tom's deteriorating mental state. The film's signature hypnosis sequences, with their rapid-fire imagery and disorienting angles, influenced later supernatural thrillers like The Ring (2002) and White Noise (2005). The psychic visions are portrayed through a distinctive blue-tinted filter and staccato editing that set it apart from contemporary ghost stories of the era.

The film's exploration of working-class paranormal experiences connects it to other supernatural thrillers that examine class dynamics, like Poltergeist (1982) and The People Under the Stairs (1991). Where many ghost stories focus on wealthy families in massive haunted mansions, Stir of Echoes brings supernatural horror to cramped apartments and neighborhood bars, making the terror more relatable and immediate. movies.title: Frailty
movies.slug: A father believes he's been commanded by God to kill demons disguised as humans

sections.content: The film's strength lies in its portrayal of psychic abilities as a burden rather than a gift. Unlike the composed psychics of The Dead Zone (1983) or Minority Report (2002), Tom's abilities manifest as an assault on his sanity, destroying his job performance and family life. Kevin Bacon's performance captures the exhaustion and desperation of a man whose mind has become a receiver for traumatic echoes he never asked to hear.
